items.title: The Three Refinements Mapped: From the First Dhyāna to Mastery of the Superknowledges

items.zh: 欲等尋思障出家者，令其不能心生喜樂。親等尋思障憙樂者，令其不能恒修善法。由斷彼故，恒修善法，速得圓滿純淨之心，有尋有伺，如淨金沙，是名為心除垢陶鍊。猶如生金仍未銷煮。
items.en: The thoughts of desire and the rest [ill-will, harm] obstruct the renunciant, preventing joy and bliss from arising in the mind. The thoughts of kinsfolk and the rest obstruct that joy and bliss, preventing sustained cultivation of wholesome dharmas. By severing these, one sustains the cultivation of wholesome dharmas and swiftly attains a perfectly pure mind, with applied and sustained thought — like pure gold-sand. This is called the mind's refining that removes impurities — like raw gold not yet smelted.

items.zh: 若有復能止息尋思，乃至具足安住第四靜慮，是名為心攝受陶鍊。由能攝受無尋無伺三摩地故。猶如生金已被銷煮。若三摩地不為有行之所拘執，乃至廣說，是名為心調柔陶鍊。於神通法，隨其所欲能轉變故。如彼生金，已細鍊治瑕隙等穢。
items.en: If one can further still the discursive thoughts, up through abiding fully in the fourth dhyāna, this is called the mind's refining that consolidates, since one has taken up the concentration free of applied and sustained thought — like raw gold already smelted. If the concentration is no longer gripped by deliberate effort, and so on at length, this is called the mind's refining that softens: with regard to the superknowledges, one can transform at will, just as that raw gold, already finely worked, has every flaw and blemish removed.

items.title: Calming, Uplifting, Equanimity: Why No Single Mode of Practice Suffices Alone

items.zh: 復次，如經言：應於三相作意思惟，乃至廣說。應時時間作意思惟奢摩他等差別之相，不應一向。為欲對治沈掉等故。若於止、舉未串習者，惟一向修，是沈掉相。如此修者，當知住在方便道位。
items.en: Furthermore, as the sūtra says: one should attend to and contemplate three marks, and so on at length. One should, from time to time, attend to and contemplate the distinguishing marks of calming and the rest — not exclusively one alone — in order to counter dullness and agitation. If one is not yet practised in calming and uplifting and cultivates only one exclusively, this produces the very mark of dullness or agitation. One who practises this way should be known to still stand on the preparatory path.

items.zh: 若時時間思惟捨相，如是在於成滿道位。亦由於此一向修故，於緣起法及聖諦中不思擇故，心不正定，不盡諸漏。於諸諦中，若未現觀、不能現觀；或已現觀，不得漏盡。初之二種，是三摩地能成辦道；第三一種，依三摩地盡諸漏道；是名略顯此中要義。
items.en: If one attends from time to time to the mark of equanimity, this stands at the path's completion. Yet by exclusively cultivating [calming] alone, without discerning dependent origination and the noble truths, the mind fails to reach right concentration and does not exhaust the outflows. Regarding the truths: if one has not yet directly realised them, one cannot come to realise them; or, having already realised them, one still fails to exhaust the outflows. The first two [calming and uplifting] are the path that accomplishes concentration itself; the third [equanimity] is the path that, resting on concentration, exhausts the outflows — this briefly displays the essential meaning here.

items.zh: 於時時間作意思惟，遍一切故。

items.title: Four Things That Uphold the Teaching: Seclusion, Practice, and Their Fruit

items.zh: 復次，有四正法，攝持聖教。何等為四？一者、遠離，二者、修習，三者、修果，四者、於聖教中無有乖諍。遠離者，謂山林、樹下、空閑靜室。修習者，謂住於彼勤修二法。謂奢摩他、毘鉢舍那。
items.en: Furthermore, there are four true dharmas that uphold the noble teaching. What are the four? Seclusion, practice, the fruit of practice, and freedom from contention within the noble teaching. Seclusion means mountain forests, beneath trees, or a quiet, secluded dwelling. Practice means, abiding there, diligently cultivating the two dharmas — calm and insight.

items.zh: 云何已習奢摩他，依毘鉢舍那而得解脫？謂如有一，先已得初靜慮乃至第四靜慮。彼即依此三摩地故，如實知苦乃至知道。彼即依此毘鉢舍那，於見所斷諸煩惱中，心得解脫。云何已習毘鉢舍那，依奢摩他心得解脫？謂如有一，如實知苦乃至知道。彼依如是增上慧故，發生靜慮。即由如是奢摩他故，於修所斷諸煩惱中，心得解脫。
items.en: How does one who has practised calm gain release resting on insight? Someone who has already attained the first dhyāna up through the fourth: resting on this concentration, he truly knows suffering, up through truly knowing the path; resting on this insight, his mind gains release from the afflictions cut on the path of seeing. How does one who has practised insight gain release resting on calm in mind? Someone who truly knows suffering, up through truly knowing the path: resting on this heightened wisdom, he gives rise to dhyāna; by this very calm, his mind gains release from the afflictions cut on the path of cultivation.

items.zh: 如是修習奢摩他、毘鉢舍那已，於諸界中而得解脫。見道所斷諸行斷故，名為斷界。修道所斷諸行斷故，名離欲界。一切有執皆永滅故，名為滅界。是名修果。

items.title: No Contention Within the Teaching: Why the Buddha and Every Disciple Answer Alike

items.zh: 於聖教中無乖諍者，所謂大師及諸弟子，若義、若句、若文，於文句義平等潤洽，互相隨順；非如異道施設見解，種種非一，差別不同。
items.en: "Freedom from contention within the noble teaching" means that the Teacher and all his disciples, in meaning, in phrase, and in letter, harmonise evenly and accord with one another throughout — unlike the views set up by other paths, which are many and various, each differing from the rest.

items.zh: 第一句者，所謂前句。若以此句問於初一，即以此句而問第二。設於初一依蘊而問，復於第二依餘問者，便不得名與第一句平等潤洽，互相隨順。
items.en: The "first statement" is what is called the preceding statement. If one questions the first person with this statement, one questions the second person with this very same statement. But if one questions the first person on the basis of the aggregates, and then questions the second on some other basis, this cannot be called harmonising evenly and according with the first statement.

items.title: A Major Threshold: The Ground of Meditative Equipoise Closes, and the Ground of Non-Equipoise Opens

items.zh: 已說三摩呬多地。云何非三摩呬多地？
items.en: The Ground of Non-Equipoise, the seventh in the Basic Section [of the treatise]. The Ground of Meditative Equipoise has now been explained. What is the Ground of Non-Equipoise?

blocks.text: A short reading that completes the Stage of Meditative Absorption. It ends with four things that keep the teaching alive, including harmony among practitioners, and then opens the seventh stage, the stage that is *not* meditative absorption.
As on Day 98: from the first aspiration to the first dhyāna is removing impurities; the second to fourth dhyānas, consolidating; mastery of the supernormal knowledges, softening.

Calming, uplifting, and equanimity must not be practised exclusively. Master Cháng Bǎi gives the goldsmith's version: "Blowing hard on the gold constantly may make it burn," like constant uplifting that agitates the mind; constantly sprinkling water cools it so it will not melt, like constant calming that sinks into dullness; leaving it alone entirely means it never gets refined. A smith alternates as the metal requires. So does a meditator.

subs.head: Four dharmas that uphold the teaching

blocks.text: Four true dharmas uphold the noble teaching: **seclusion**, **practice**, **the fruit of practice**, and **freedom from contention**. Venerable Miào Jìng on practice: "Of the three wisdoms, hearing and reflection aren't called cultivation; only cultivation-wisdom is." Study supports the teaching; practice keeps it alive.

Calm-first practitioners, relying on insight, are freed from the afflictions cut on the path of seeing; insight-first practitioners, generating dhyāna, are freed from those cut on the path of cultivation (Day 97).

The Buddha and every disciple answer alike when asked about the teaching. Venerable Miào Jìng quotes a saying: "When monks praise monks, the Dharma flourishes": "you don't say I'm wrong, I won't say you're wrong." Master Cháng Bǎi explains a textual detail: whichever person you ask, with whichever statement, the answer agrees.
The point is not uniformity of opinion but integrity of the teaching. Where the teachers contradict each other, students lose faith; where they agree in substance, the teaching is trusted.

"The Ground of Meditative Equipoise has been explained." Five fascicles (9 through 13, in part) on concentration end here. The seventh stage, the **Ground of Non-Equipoise** (非三摩呬多地), follows immediately and, as tomorrow shows, is very short: it is defined by what it lacks.

quiz.q: How do the three refinements map onto the dhyānas, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: from aspiration to the first dhyāna is removing impurities; the second to fourth is consolidating; mastery of the superknowledges is softening
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "From the first aspiration to the first dhyāna is refining that removes impurities; then the second, third, and fourth — complete concentration — is refining that consolidates." The text: mastery over the superknowledges is softening. Many disciples haven't finished even the first stage.

quiz.q: Calming, uplifting, and equanimity shouldn't be practised exclusively. What goldsmith simile does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: blowing constantly makes gold burn, like constant uplifting agitating the mind; constantly sprinkling water cools it, like constant calming dulling the mind
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Blowing hard on gold constantly may make it burn — like constantly uplifting, agitating the mind"; "constantly sprinkling it with water may cool it — like constantly calming, dimming the mind." Venerable Miào Jìng: equanimity is calm and insight together.

quiz.q: According to the treatise, what four true dharmas uphold the noble teaching?
options: seclusion, practice, its fruit, and freedom from contention within the teaching
quiz.why: "Seclusion, practice, the fruit of practice, and freedom from contention within the noble teaching." Venerable Miào Jìng: a temple's abbot is called 住持 — one who upholds the teaching so it doesn't perish.

quiz.q: "Practice" means diligently cultivating calm and insight in seclusion. Which of the three wisdoms counts as "practice," per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: hearing and reflection aren't "practice"; only cultivation-wisdom is
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Of the three wisdoms, hearing and reflection aren't called cultivation; only cultivation-wisdom is." Attaining the fourth dhyāna without contemplating the truths is calm without insight.

quiz.q: Which afflictions are released in each: calm-first relying on insight, and insight-first relying on calm?
options: calm-first, relying on insight, is freed from afflictions cut by seeing; insight-first, generating dhyāna, is freed from those cut by cultivation
quiz.why: "Resting on this insight, his mind gains release from the afflictions cut on the path of seeing"; "by this very calm, his mind gains release from the afflictions cut on the path of cultivation." Venerable Miào Jìng: the second route achieves insight within threshold concentration.

quiz.q: Freedom from contention means teacher and disciples harmonise. What saying does Venerable Miào Jìng cite?
options: "when monks praise monks, the Dharma flourishes" — don't say I'm wrong, I won't say you're wrong
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "Then it's said, 'when monks praise monks, the Dharma flourishes' — you don't say I'm wrong, I don't say you're wrong." Patriarchs' sayings may be studied, but the Buddha's sūtras keep one on course.
